olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Determine all nonneg­ative integer solutions $(n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_{14})$, apart from permutations, of $n_1^4+n_2^4+\cdots+n_{14}^4=1599$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1979

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $S$ be a great circle with pole $P$. On any great circle through $P$, two points $A,B$ are chosen equidistant from $P$. For any spherical triangle $ABC$ with $C$ on $S$, prove that arc $CP$ bisects angle $C$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1979

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Given three identical $n$-faced dice with faces numbered arbitrarily, prove that the probability that the sum of the bottom three faces is divisible by 3 is at least $1/4$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1979

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Show how to construct a chord $BPC$ of a given angle $A$ through a given point $P$ such that $\frac{1}{BP}+\frac{1}{PC}$ is maximum.
figure_description: An angle A with point P inside and chord BPC through P
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1979

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: An organization has $n$ members and $n+1$ three-member committees, no two with identical membership. Prove there are two committees sharing exactly one member.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1979
